Use set extensionality and reduce every equality to pointwise membership. The maps involved are order embeddings:

- `Fin.natAdd n m` shifts values by `m`, so
  \[
  m+i \le m+x \iff i\le x,\qquad m+x<m+j\iff x<j.
  \]
  Thus the preimage of `Ico (natAdd i) (natAdd j)` is exactly `Ico i j`.

- `Fin.val` reflects order. After unfolding membership in `uIcc` as the disjunction of the two possible endpoint orderings, all inequalities are equivalent to the corresponding inequalities in `Fin n`.

- `Fin.castSucc` preserves values and reflects order, so
  \[
  \operatorname{castSucc}(x)\le\operatorname{castSucc}(i)\iff x\le i,
  \]
  giving the stated preimage identity for `Iic`.

Organize the proof by first proving the `natAdd` equality, then proving both sides of the displayed `Iff` independently by `Set.ext` and simplification of interval membership. Since both universally quantified statements are true, conclude their equivalence directly. Empty `Fin n` cases require no special treatment because the endpoint quantifiers are then vacuous.
